jobs.title: Director– Data Governance (ELT Delegate Engagement Program Lead)
jobs.description:
Title: Director– Data Governance (ELT Delegate Engagement Program Lead)

Location: Toronto, ON (3 Days/Week from Office and 2 days Remote)

Duration: 6 to 12+ Months (Possibility of Extension)

Start : ASAP

The expected base salary range for this position is $80/HR - $90/HR, depending on experience, skills, and internal equity. The Company offers a total rewards package in accordance with all applicable federal, provincial, and local laws and requirements. Benefit eligibility and offerings vary based on role, employment status, and work location.

For contractor positions, benefits are limited to those entitlements and protections required by applicable law, which may include (as applicable) vacation pay, public holidays, leaves of absence, and other legally mandated benefits or payments. We may use AI-enabled and/or automated tools to support parts of our recruitment process, including application screening, interview scheduling, and candidate communications. These tools are used to enhance consistency and efficiency. All hiring decisions involve human review and are not based solely on automated processing.

Position Overview

Client is seeking a Program Lead to drive the activation and execution of the ELT Delegate Engagement Program.

This role will lead a high-visibility enterprise initiative focused on strengthening business accountability for data risk, data quality, and data governance across global segments and functions.

The ideal candidate will have strong enterprise program management, data governance, executive stakeholder engagement, and change leadership experience within a complex and regulated organization.

Key Responsibilities

1. ELT Delegate Activation Program

Lead day-to-day execution of the ELT Delegate Engagement Program.
Manage activation plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and outcomes.
Drive delegate onboarding through sustained adoption of the governance operating model.
Coordinate activities across multiple business segments and functions.

2. Executive Stakeholder Management

Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, ELT Delegates, Data Owners, Data Stewards, and governance teams.
Lead executive onboarding, workshops, working sessions, and briefings.
Influence stakeholders, remove barriers, and drive timely decision-making.
Communicate complex governance topics in clear, business-focused language.

3. Data Governance & Program Facilitation

Facilitate data landscape assessments to identify:
Critical data
Data ownership
Dependencies
Governance gaps
Data risks
Establish and support local Data Governance Forums.
Drive resolution and escalation of data risks, issues, ownership, and accountability gaps.
Support implementation of governance decision rights, accountabilities, and escalation paths.

4. Executive Reporting & Communications

Prepare executive presentations, leadership briefings, status reports, dashboards, and metrics.
Track program progress and provide recommendations and escalations.
Translate program activities into measurable business outcomes and risk reduction.
Provide leadership with clear visibility into progress, risks, and decisions required.

5. Change Leadership & Adoption

Drive adoption and sustained participation in data governance practices.
Embed governance activities into business operating rhythms and decision-making forums.
Improve governance activation processes, tools, templates, and operating practices.
Ensure governance strategy and policies are translated into practical business processes and controls.

Must-Have Qualifications

5+ years of experience leading:
Enterprise Data Governance programs
Data Management programs
Data Transformation programs
Related enterprise transformation initiatives
Experience working within a complex and/or regulated organization.
Strong executive communication, presentation, and facilitation skills.
Proven experience influencing senior leadership and executive stakeholders.
Strong experience managing complex, multi-workstream enterprise programs from concept through execution.
Strong knowledge of Data Governance principles and practices, including:
Data ownership & stewardship
Critical data identification
Data quality
Metadata & data lineage
Data issue management
Data controls
Data risk
Experience designing, implementing, or operationalizing enterprise data governance operating models.
Experience with governance forums, decision rights, accountability models, standards, and escalation processes.
Ability to translate data governance strategy/policy into practical business processes, controls, and measurable outcomes.
Strong program management, organization, coordination, and follow-through skills.

Nice-to-Have

Financial services/insurance industry experience.
Experience in a highly matrixed global organization.
Experience working directly with ELT / executive-level stakeholders.
Experience driving enterprise-wide change management and adoption.
Familiarity with program management methodologies and tools.
Experience connecting data governance initiatives to business value, risk reduction, and measurable outcomes.

Benefits:

“The Company offers a total rewards package for this position that may include employer-sponsored benefits, where applicable and subject to eligibility requirements, such as supplemental health and dental coverage, life insurance, disability insurance, retirement or savings programs, paid time off, and other benefits.
The availability, structure, and scope of benefits may vary based on role, employment status, work location, and applicable federal and provincial laws. The Company provides all statutory entitlements, including public holidays, vacation, leaves of absence, and government-mandated benefits, in accordance with applicable law"

These tools are used to enhance consistency and efficiency. All hiring decisions involve human review and are not based solely on automated processing"

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Our Client

Our client is a leading law firm in downtown Toronto
seeking a Director of Finance & Accounting
to join its Finance team. Reporting to senior Finance leadership and working closely with executive stakeholders, the successful candidate will lead an established team while identifying opportunities to strengthen processes, controls, reporting and overall revenue performance. This is an excellent opportunity for a hands-on, solutions-oriented finance leader
who enjoys both strategic oversight and getting into the details.

The role is four days per week in office in downtown Toronto
and offers a competitive compensation package.

Responsibilities
Provide end-to-end leadership of the revenue lifecycle, including WIP, billing, e-billing, rates administration, accounts receivable, collections, cash application and revenue reporting
.
Lead annual revenue planning, budgeting and forecasting and provide financial insights to support strategic and operational decision-making.
Develop and monitor key revenue and working-capital metrics, identifying trends, risks and opportunities to improve financial performance.
Drive strategies to improve realization, accelerate billing and collections, reduce aged WIP and receivables, and enhance cash flow.
Oversee billing arrangements, rate administration, alternative fee arrangements and e-billing processes.
Develop management reporting, dashboards and business intelligence solutions that provide meaningful and actionable insights.
Lead process-improvement, automation and finance-transformation initiatives
, including system implementations, upgrades and optimization projects.
Partner with Technology, Finance and other internal stakeholders to improve data quality, reporting efficiency and system utilization.
Lead, mentor and develop the revenue operations team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Present financial information and recommendations to senior leadership and other key stakeholders in a clear and commercially focused manner.

Requirements
CPA designation required.

10+ years of progressive finance experience
, including meaningful leadership responsibilities.
Strong experience in revenue operations, FP&A, billing, rates, accounts receivable and/or collections
.
Demonstrated experience leading teams and driving process improvement, systems implementation and organizational change
.
Experience within a professional services environment
strongly preferred; law firm, accounting or consulting experience would be particularly relevant.
Strong financial planning, reporting, analytical and business acumen.
Advanced proficiency with Excel, financial modelling, dashboards and business intelligence tools
; Power BI experience is an asset.
Experience with ERP or practice-management systems and system implementations/upgrades; Aderant experience is an asset
.
A hands-on, solutions-oriented leadership style with the ability to balance strategic thinking with attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the presence and credibility to work directly with senior stakeholders.
Ability to simplify complex financial information and communicate effectively with non-financial audiences.

jobs.title: Chief Financial & Risk Officer (CFRO)
jobs.description:
Job Function

In support of the Mission and Vision of Motor City Community Credit Union, the Chief Financial and Risk Officer (CFRO) is responsible for leading and managing the financial stewardship of the organization to ensure fiscal responsibility and maintain financial readiness. The CFRO is also responsible for the oversight of Motor City Community Credit Union’s Enterprise Risk Management regime and will be the contact person to the Board of Directors as it relates to risk.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide leadership, direction and financial/risk expertise to the organization, with responsibility for corporate finance structure, financial reporting, forecasting and business planning, risk management, setting financial policies and establishing financial targets to effectively measure success
Direct the overall forecasting, planning & analysis, accounting, budgeting, financial reporting and the overall evaluation of the business
Ensure timely and accurate financial and compliance reports for management and the Board of Directors, external auditors and regulators
Accountable for Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) practice, ensuring all programs are in compliance including capital risk management, structural risk management, market risk management and liquidity risk management
Collaborate with the senior leadership team and Board of Directors in establishing key risk indicators, tolerance levels and monitoring trends
Oversee the compliance function including anti-money laundering and all Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada ( FINTRAC) requirements
Responsible for the compliance governance function including all support for the Board, Committees and individual directors
Serve as key point of contact for the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) relationship manager including responding to all requests
Act as the point person between the Credit Union and the Board of Directors as it relates to risk,
Develop the long-term financial forecast plan that aligns with the Credit Union’s strategic and business plans
Oversee the finance and compliance departments and provide strategic leadership and mentorship to the team
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree in Business or Equivalent
Accounting Designation (CPA)
10-15 years’ experience in a Financial Services environment (Credit Union experience an asset)
4-5 years of Senior Management experience
Anti-money laundering/Anti-terrorist financing experience an asset
Enterprise Risk Management facilitation considered an asset
Must be bondable

Competencies/Skills:

Strong knowledge of IFRS reporting standards
Strong knowledge of the Credit Union and Caisse Populaires Act, 2020
Development and/or maintenance of administrative and financial policies and procedures
Senior level oversight of AML/ATF regime
Proven ability to work closely with a Board of Directors and Regulators
Strong attention to detail and analytical skills
Experience in strategic planning and execution
Strong leadership, interpersonal, communication and relationship building skills
Proficient in time management, written and verbal communication skills
Excellent organizational and planning skills
Ability to perform under pressure and work independently
Ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines as required
Computer proficient in Microsoft Office such as Word and Excel
Experience working in a unionized work environment an asset

Motor City Community Credit Union endeavours to accommodate the needs of candidates under the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act [AODA] throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. If contacted for an interview, please advise if you require accommodation.
Motor City Community Credit Union is committed to equity of employment. As an equal opportunity employer, we would like to thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
In accordance with applicable employment legislation, Motor City Community Credit Union confirms that it does not use artificial intelligence or automated screening tools as part of its recruitment or candidate assessment processes. All candidate applications are reviewed and assessed by members of our hiring team.
In accordance with applicable job posting transparency requirements, this posting is for an existing vacancy at Motor City Community Credit Union.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Collectivfide Insurance Group brings together the entrepreneurial energy of a growing start up with the strength, heritage, and community-focused values of the Mutual insurance companies that support us.
We have ambitious plans to double our size over the next five years through a combination of M&A, organic growth, and operational excellence. We are seeking a strategic and forward-thinking CFO to help shape the financial strategy and build a scalable infrastructure required for our next stage of growth.  

This is a high-impact opportunity to define the financial strategy, build and lead a high performing finance team while strengthening the systems, structure, and capabilities needed to scale, optimize capital and profitability, and help drive value through both organic growth and M&A to bring our vision to life.

The ideal candidate brings enterprise-level perspective, strategic capabilities with the willingness to remain close to the details.

So what will you be doing?

Enterprise Strategy & Value Creation

Partner with the CEO and Board to define and execute the company's long-term growth strategy.
Evaluate strategic alternatives including acquisitions, partnerships, capital investments, and new business opportunities.
 Lead enterprise-wide scenario planning and strategic financial analysis.
 Identify and improve the key drivers of shareholder value.
Provide independent challenge and insight to executive decision-making.
Assess the current state in relations to strategy alignment, governance and compliance, making recommendations that will enable scalability and long-term success. 
Analyze the company’s cash flow and liquidity position, ensuring optimal cash utilization and availability at all times. Utilize key performance metrics such as IRR, WACC to inform decision making.

M&A & Capital Raise

Accountable for ensuring acquisitions deliver expected financial and strategic outcomes through post-acquisition performance measurement, value realization tracking, and ongoing portfolio review
Create and maintain financial models and forecast as well as conduct scenario analysis to support strategic decision making and evaluate current and potential investment opportunities.
Manage and optimize the company’s current and future cash flow, including preparing the company to raise the capital it needs to support its cash requirements and growth plans. This can range from securing loans, pursuing external capital, financial modelling and scenario analysis and M&A activities.
Prepare investor presentations to facilitate discussions with capital markets participants, investors, and lending vendors.

Financial Performance Accountability

Establish and monitor enterprise KPIs linked to growth, EBITDA, cash flow, capital efficiency, and shareholder returns.
Lead quarterly business performance reviews with executive leadership.
Drive accountability for financial performance across all operating companies.
Ensure business leaders understand the financial drivers of their results and are taking action to improve them.
Monitor and manage the company’s debt portfolio, including debt analysis, issuance, repayment, and refinancing.
Support the preparation and execution of equity and debt offering, including due diligence, valuation, and pricing.
Understand the company’s tax requirements and implement optimal tax strategies for the entire group of companies.
Provide financial expertise, reporting, risk mitigation and recommendations to the Board and investors and other stakeholders.
Ensure there are scalable financial processes, procedures, controls and solutions in place to support growth plans, drive efficiency and ensure compliance.

Leadership

Operate as an enterprise executive first and a finance leader second.
Demonstrate strong commercial and strategic thinking.
Develop and lead a unified team. 
Collaborates across departments to steer corporate change/financial strategy.
Aligns stakeholders and motivates the team around the company vision.
Effectively challenge assumptions and influence executive and Board decision-making.
Balance short-term financial performance with long-term value creation.
Build capability & leadership bench strength within the finance function to allow the CFO to focus on strategy and growth.

Qualifications

University degree in accounting, finance, business administration.
MBA, CPA designation.
Minimum 7 years of financial leadership in the insurance industry (preferred), with previous CFO experience, including hands on experience in building the financial strategy and structure to scale a business that balances operational growth and M&A.
Proven track record in the areas of corporate finance including: investor relations, financial modelling, investment banking or capital markets.
Previous experience leading a capital raise and dealing with investors and shareholders.
Prior success working in the private sector with a large subsidiary base, dealing with cash management to fund M&A and generate long-term profits. 
Practical experience in raising equity and debt financing and communication with banks, investors and other financial stakeholders.
Advanced knowledge of the concepts, principles and practices pertaining to corporate finance planning, analysis and reporting.
Hands on experience building and maintaining complex financial models. 
Must have strong communication and organizational skills and be able to multi-task and manage multiple projects simultaneously.

Your final salary will be based on your experience, skills, qualifications, and the value you bring to the role.

Of course, great compensation is about more than salary. We offer a competitive total rewards package that includes comprehensive health and dental benefits, employer pension matching, generous vacation time, personal days, volunteer days, and Pawreavement Leave, because we know pets are family, too.

Real People, Real Conversations, Real Hiring

jobs.title: Director, AI Delivery
jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you'll be doing

Our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) team within Operations helps turn high-value opportunities into practical solutions that improve how work gets done across the business. As the Director, AI Delivery, you'll lead the end-to-end delivery of a growing portfolio of AI and Generative AI initiatives, from opportunity identification and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization. You'll lead and develop a team of data scientists while creating the structure, operating rhythm, and accountability needed to deliver consistently in a complex enterprise environment. Working closely with Operations leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll translate business problems into clear, well-scoped initiatives with measurable outcomes. You'll also manage competing priorities across the portfolio, remove barriers to progress, and help ensure solutions are successfully embedded into business workflows. Success in this role means building a delivery organization that scales effectively, delivers predictably, and creates measurable business impact.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed

Lead delivery excellence
- Own the end-to-end delivery of the Operations AI portfolio, from intake and prioritization through development, production, adoption, and realized value. Create clear ownership, execution discipline, and accountability across initiatives.
Build trusted business partnerships
- Partner closely with Operations leaders and teams to understand business needs, identify high-value AI opportunities, and shape a sustainable pipeline of use cases with clear outcomes and success measures.
Manage the portfolio
- Continuously assess and prioritize concurrent AI initiatives based on business value, feasibility, capacity, dependencies, and evolving insights. Make pragmatic decisions on scope, sequencing, resourcing, and delivery approach to maintain momentum.
Navigate enterprise delivery
- Drive initiatives forward with partners across data science, engineering, technology, risk, governance, and the business. Anticipate blockers and dependencies early, and work across the organization to resolve them.
Embed solutions for impact -
Ensure AI solutions don't stop at production and are effectively adopted into business workflows to achieve intended outcomes. Create transparency into delivery progress, risks, capacity, portfolio health, and business value.
Develop your team -
Lead, coach, and support a team of data scientists across multiple levels of experience. Help team members build ownership, strengthen stakeholder management, and increase delivery effectiveness over time.

Who you are

You are a caring and accountable leader
. You have experience developing and leading teams responsible for delivering complex technology or AI initiatives. You create clarity and accountability while empowering talented people to take ownership of their work.
You can demonstrate experience in
delivering Generative AI solutions in a business environment, portfolio delivery, and cross-functional execution across business and technology teams. It’s an asset if you also bring broader experience in artificial intelligence and machine learning delivery.
You give meaning to data
. You understand enough about AI and Generative AI delivery to challenge assumptions, identify delivery risks, and work effectively with data scientists and engineers. You balance technical understanding with strong business judgment.
Your influence makes a difference
. You're comfortable working directly with senior business leaders and building trusted relationships across diverse partner groups. You can challenge priorities, scope, and expectations in a constructive and effective way.
You act like an owner
. You focus on business outcomes, adoption, and value realization rather than activity alone. You make thoughtful trade-offs, know when to accelerate or reshape work, and can stop initiatives that aren't delivering enough value.
Values matter to you
. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

Our AI team builds enterprise capabilities that support a wide range of users across the organization, from end users to technology teams and low-code or no-code builders. Build scalable engineering foundations

Define and implement standards for code structure, testing, code review, versioning, packaging, documentation, release management, and production readiness for AI and Generative AI products.

- Create automated testing, evaluation, regression, monitoring, and observability patterns that support both traditional software quality and the unique behavior of probabilistic AI systems.

- Establish continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) patterns, quality gates, and repeatable workflows that help teams move from experiment to production with greater speed and consistency.

- Review architecture and code for critical products, coach AI practitioners on engineering best practices, and help the team adopt effective agentic development workflows, tooling, and guardrails.

. You understand the engineering challenges of taking AI and Generative AI solutions from experimentation into production, and you know that quality for AI systems requires more than traditional unit testing.
You look beyond the moment.
You're excited by the opportunity to shape how agentic software development evolves, including workflows, repository design, testing approaches, review practices, context management, and governance for increasingly autonomous delivery.
You're motivated by collective success
. You influence engineers, data scientists, technology partners, and leaders through strong partnership, sound judgment, and a commitment to raising the capability of the broader organization.
You act like an owner
. You naturally identify repeated patterns, remove friction from the development lifecycle, and build practical solutions that help teams deliver faster, more safely, and with greater consistency.
Values matter to you
. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

new_jobs.title: Director, AI Engineering, Principal Product Scaler
new_jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you'll be doing

Our AI team builds enterprise capabilities that support a wide range of users across the organization, from end users to technology teams and low-code or no-code builders. As a Principal Product Scaler – AI Engineering, you'll build the engineering foundation that helps us repeatedly deliver high-quality AI products safely, efficiently, and at scale. You'll architect and develop the reusable components, software development kits, testing frameworks, and delivery patterns that move us from individual implementations to a mature product engineering model. You'll establish the standards for how AI products are designed, built, tested, packaged, released, and monitored in production. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, and technology partners, you'll help turn strong prototypes into reliable enterprise products while strengthening the team's overall engineering capability.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed

Build scalable engineering foundations
- Design and develop software development kits, libraries, reusable components, templates, and reference implementations that accelerate delivery across the AI portfolio and reduce repeated effort across teams.
Establish engineering excellence -
Define and implement standards for code structure, testing, code review, versioning, packaging, documentation, release management, and production readiness for AI and Generative AI products.
Advance AI quality and reliability
- Create automated testing, evaluation, regression, monitoring, and observability patterns that support both traditional software quality and the unique behavior of probabilistic AI systems.
Drive efficient delivery
- Establish continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) patterns, quality gates, and repeatable workflows that help teams move from experiment to production with greater speed and consistency.
Enable adoption across teams -
Design interfaces and developer experiences that make enterprise AI capabilities easy to consume for technology teams, other AI teams, and low-code or no-code solution builders.
Elevate team capability
- Review architecture and code for critical products, coach AI practitioners on engineering best practices, and help the team adopt effective agentic development workflows, tooling, and guardrails.

Who you are

You are a hands-on senior engineering leader
. You have experience operating at a Staff, Principal, Lead Engineer, or equivalent level, and you enjoy both designing systems and writing production-quality code.
You can demonstrate experience in
system design, application programming interface (API) and software development kit (SDK) design, testing, CI/CD, versioning, observability, and production operations. It’s an asset if you have built platforms, frameworks, developer tooling, or reusable services used by multiple teams.
You give meaning to data
. You understand the engineering challenges of taking AI and Generative AI solutions from experimentation into production, and you know that quality for AI systems requires more than traditional unit testing.
You look beyond the moment.
You're excited by the opportunity to shape how agentic software development evolves, including workflows, repository design, testing approaches, review practices, context management, and governance for increasingly autonomous delivery.
You're motivated by collective success
. You influence engineers, data scientists, technology partners, and leaders through strong partnership, sound judgment, and a commitment to raising the capability of the broader organization.
You act like an owner
. You naturally identify repeated patterns, remove friction from the development lifecycle, and build practical solutions that help teams deliver faster, more safely, and with greater consistency.
Values matter to you
. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills tests (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency, MS Office). Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.
